title: Introduce stochastic temporal surgeon and cost-aware prefill synthesizer
author: Priya Desai
description:
Motivation: Long-tail cost and latency events are often seeded by poor KV-cache priming and temporal clustering of rare long responses. This PR adds a compact "stochastic temporal surgeon" runner that synthesizes skewed-length session traces and a cost-aware prefill synthesizer that tries different prefill budgets to measure KV-cache efficacy vs. token-cost tradeoffs.

What this PR contains: - New runner `temporal_surgeon` that emits session traces with controllable long-tail injection (frequency, amplitude, burst-width) and optional per-session primer sequences. - Cost-aware prefill component (harness + Python evaluation) that experiments with prefix budgets and reports token-cost vs P95 latency and quality deltas. - Compact reporting pipeline that produces a Phase Alignment Heatmap (compact NDJSON) mapping token-phase occupancy to kernel-level hotpoints for quick triage. - CI integration: lightweight end-to-end smoke tests and a resource-limited integration test for the runner so it can be exercised on CI without large infra.

Why unique: unlike previous burst/replayer tools, this focuses on (1) surgical long-tail insertion at epoch boundaries, (2) coupling cost-models into prefill strategy permutation testing, and (3) a small, human-readably compact heatmap format intended for rapid on-call inspection and automated alerting.

Usage: see README at benchmark-lab/runners/temporal_surgeon/README.md for example CLI invocations and sample config YML. Typical invocation: `bl-runner temporal-surgeon --seed 42 --longtail-rate 0.02 --burst-width 8 --prefill-budget 32`

Notes: this is intentionally small-footprint; the runtime runner is written in Rust with a thin Python harness for result aggregation and cost-model sweeps. The PR includes benchmark vectors used in our internal perf-suite and a short tutorial notebook for exploratory analysis.
commit_summary: init: add temporal_surgeon runner (rust) with core injection logic
feat: add cost-aware prefill synthesizer and python harness for sweeps
test: add unit+smoke tests for runner deterministic modes
docs: README and example configs + notebook for heatmap interpretation
ci: add minimal integration job and resource caps for GitHub Actions
review_comments: Ben Liu: Nice compact design. Request: add an option to output per-token primer metadata so we can correlate with KV-hit traces in perf pipelines.
Priya Desai (author): Added `--emit-primer-meta` flag and included a sample correlation script under `metrics_collector.py`.
Yuna Park: The heatmap format looks useful but we should standardize field names. Suggest `phase_id` -> `phase_idx` and include `kernel_hint` explicit enum.
Priya Desai: Renamed field to `phase_idx` and added `kernel_hint` enum with values ["softmax", "matmul", "attention"] in serializer. Added tests for roundtrip parsing.
Marco Rossi: CI integration failed initially due to container resource limits; please cap parallelism on the runner when `CI_MODE` env var is set.
Priya Desai: Added `CI_MODE` gating and reduced worker-count in the smoke workflow; re-ran CI and green.
Yuna Park: Approving after addressing field standardization and small code comments.
Ben Liu: Approved. Observability team will pick up heatmap alerts mapping next sprint.
release_notes: Introduce temporal_surgeon runner and cost-aware prefill synthesizer. Adds Phase Alignment Heatmap reporter for compact long-tail triage. Useful for regression tests that measure token-cost vs P95 latency tradeoffs.
